content: Store this medication at room temperature, ensuring it is kept away from moisture and light. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Liquid forms of this medication should not be frozen. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the product is expired or no longer needed, discard it properly according to local regulations. This information was last updated in May 2024. It is important to note that this document provides a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. To use this medication, follow all instructions provided on the product packaging. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, take it exactly as directed. This medication is to be taken orally, with or without food. For liquid forms, use a special measuring device or spoon to ensure accurate dosing. Do not use a household spoon, as it may result in an incorrect dose. The dosage is determined based on your age, medical condition, and response to treatment. Common side effects may include drowsiness, constipation, blurred vision, or dryness of the mouth, nose, or throat. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before taking dimenhydrinate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to diphenhydramine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause drowsiness or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Liquid products or chewable tablets may contain sugar and/or aspartame. Exercise caution if you have diabetes, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any other condition requiring dietary restrictions. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this medication. Older adults may also be more susceptible to side effects such as drowsiness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels of all your medications, such as allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as allergy skin tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if someone exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Symptoms of overdose may include severe drowsiness, seizures, or widened pupils. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up.
